subject: social_science

concepts.title: The Globe and Earth's Axis
concepts.definition: A globe is a scaled-down physical representation of the Earth, featuring an imaginary line called an axis around which it rotates.
concepts.key_idea: The globe serves as a miniature, accurate model of our planet's shape and rotation.
question_patterns: What is a globe?
Define the axis of the earth.
In which direction does the globe rotate?
Describe the true model of the earth.
How is the earth's axis represented on a globe?

solution_steps.explain: A globe is a miniature form or true model of the earth.
The needle or imaginary line passing through the poles is the axis.

concepts.title: Equator and Hemispheres
concepts.definition: The equator is an imaginary circular line that splits the Earth into two equal parts: the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
concepts.key_idea: The equator is the primary reference line for dividing the Earth horizontally.
question_patterns: What is the equator?
Name the two hemispheres created by the equator.
What is the latitudinal value of the equator?
Which line divides the earth into northern and southern halves?
Define the Northern Hemisphere.

solution_steps.explain: The equator is the 0 degree latitude line.
The part above is the Northern Hemisphere and the part below is the Southern Hemisphere.

concepts.title: Parallels of Latitude
concepts.definition: Horizontal circles drawn parallel to the equator extending toward the poles, used to measure distance in degrees north or south.
concepts.key_idea: Latitudes are parallel circles that decrease in size as they move from the equator to the poles.
question_patterns: What are parallels of latitude?
How are latitudes measured?
What does 90 degrees North latitude represent?
Why do we use N or S with latitude values?
How does the size of parallels change towards the poles?

solution_steps.explain: All parallel circles from the equator to the poles are latitudes.
They are measured in degrees, with N for North and S for South.

concepts.title: Important Parallels of Latitude
concepts.definition: Specific latitudinal lines including the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn, and the Arctic and Antarctic Circles, which mark climate boundaries.
concepts.key_idea: Four key latitudes besides the equator and poles define the Earth's major zones.
question_patterns: List the four important parallels of latitude.
What is the value of the Tropic of Cancer?
Where is the Arctic Circle located?
What is the latitude of the Tropic of Capricorn?
Identify the parallel at 66.5 degrees South.

solution_steps.explain: Tropic of Cancer (23.5 N) and Arctic Circle (66.5 N).
Tropic of Capricorn (23.5 S) and Antarctic Circle (66.5 S).

concepts.title: Heat Zones of the Earth
concepts.definition: Regions categorized by the amount of solar heat received, classified into Torrid, Temperate, and Frigid zones.
concepts.key_idea: The angle of sun rays determines the temperature and classification of heat zones.
question_patterns: What are the three heat zones of the Earth?
Why is the Torrid Zone the hottest?
Describe the Frigid Zone.
Which zone lies between the Tropic of Cancer and the Arctic Circle?
What characterizes the Temperate Zone?

solution_steps.explain: Area between the two tropics receiving vertical sun rays.
Area between tropics and circles with moderate sun angles.
Area between circles and poles with very slanting rays.

concepts.title: Meridians of Longitude
concepts.definition: Vertical reference lines running from the North Pole to the South Pole used to measure East-West positions.
concepts.key_idea: Longitudes are semi-circles of equal length that meet at the poles.
question_patterns: What are meridians of longitude?
How is the distance between longitudes measured?
Where do all meridians meet?
Contrast latitudes and longitudes.
What happens to the distance between longitudes at the poles?

solution_steps.explain: Lines of reference running from North to South Pole.
They are semi-circles and distance between them becomes zero at poles.

concepts.title: Prime Meridian and Hemispheres
concepts.definition: The 0 degree longitude line passing through Greenwich, dividing the Earth into Eastern and Western Hemispheres.
concepts.key_idea: The Prime Meridian and the 180 degree meridian together divide the Earth vertically.
question_patterns: What is the Prime Meridian?
Where is the British Royal Observatory located?
What is the value of the Prime Meridian?
Which hemispheres are created by the Prime Meridian?
What is unique about the 180 degree East and West meridians?

solution_steps.explain: The Prime Meridian passes through Greenwich.
It divides Earth into Eastern (E) and Western (W) Hemispheres.

concepts.title: Time Difference Calculation
concepts.definition: Calculating the time gap between two locations based on the Earth's rotation rate of 4 minutes per degree of longitude.
concepts.key_idea: Earth rotates 1 degree every 4 minutes, making time dependent on longitudinal position.
question_patterns: Calculate the time difference for 15 degrees of longitude.
How many minutes does the earth take to rotate 1 degree?
If it is 12 noon at Greenwich, what is the time at 15 degrees East?
Find the time at 30 degrees West if Greenwich is at noon.
How much time difference is there for 1 degree of longitude?

solution_steps.explain: Identify the number of degrees between the two locations.
The earth rotates 1 degree in 4 minutes.

concepts.title: Indian Standard Time (IST)
concepts.section: WHY DO WE HAVE STANDARD TIME?
concepts.definition: The uniform time adopted for the whole of India based on the central meridian of 82.5 degrees East.
concepts.key_idea: Standard time prevents confusion caused by local time differences across a large country.
question_patterns: What is the Standard Meridian of India?
What is the time difference between IST and GMT?
Why does India have a standard time?
Calculate the time in India if it is 12 noon in London.
What is the full form of IST?

solution_steps.explain: India's standard meridian is 82.5 degrees East.
Multiply longitude by 4 minutes per degree.
Divide total minutes by 60 to get the hour difference.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Calculate the time difference in minutes for a place located {longitude_diff} degrees away from Greenwich.
What is the time offset in hours for India's standard meridian of {lon} degrees East?
